newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FOCUS-Norilsk Nickel union adopts strike plan.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Norilsk Nickel union adopts strike plan.

text.p: Workers at the flagship plant of Russia's giant Norilsk Nickel NKEL.RTS group approved a strike plan over salary and holiday arrears, in a move that could hit world supplies of key metals, a union spokesman said on Monday.

Boris Degtyaryov, deputy head of the plant's United Trade Union committee, told Reuters from the Arctic town of Norilsk where the plant is based that management had 10 days to answer workers' demand to avert disruption to output.
"It (the committee) has adopted its legitimate right to hold a strike," he said. "The company management has 10 days in which to resolve the situation."
Norilsk Nickel is a major supplier of nickel, cobalt and platinum group metals to world markets. It accounts for nearly 20 percent of annual world nickel supply and 60 percent of palladium supplies.
Benchmark prices of nickel, platinum and palladium have risen in recent weeks on concerns over Norilsk supplies.
The strike decision followed a meeting on March 1 of union and management representatives in the town of Norilsk, 200 miles (320 km) north of the Arctic Circle.
A Moscow-based spokesman for the RAO Norilsky Nickel 0#NKEL.RUO group said he had no comment on the union's decision or on the outcome of the March 1 talks.

Norilsk Nickel management said on Friday that it viewed any labour strike at the main plant as a move that could scupper a repayment schedule for workers' arrears. Degtyaryov said the timing of any strike and the number of workers involved still had to be decided by a committee which is coordinating talks with management.

But he said at least 50,000 workers involved in production and processing of non-ferrous and precious metals could lay down their tools. The maximum number of workers involved would be 120,000 -- the plant's entire workforce.

Norilsk's main shareholder, big commercial bank Uneximbank, is struggling to implement a rescue package for the Soviet-era metals monolith, which was a showpiece of the Communist planned economy and Moscow's drive to tap metals reserves at any cost.
Degtyaryov said it was not too late to resolve the dispute, adding that the committee should do everything to continue a dialogue with management.
"A perfect outcome would be that if all our legitimate demands were met -- there would be no strike," he said.
Russia feeds 25 to 30 percent of western European nickel demand. Stainless steel is the main end-use for nickel, and accounts for around two thirds of nickel consumption.
Norilsky Nickel owes workers 900 billion roubles ($160 million) in salary and holiday arrears and 1.2 billion roubles ($211 million) to various budgets.
Workers at the plant have also demanded wages be increased by what a RAO Norilsky Nickel spokesman said earlier would cost the company 70 billion roubles a month.
The main metals plant last year produced 100,000 tonnes of nickel from the group's total output of 177,185 tonnes. Total world production is around one million tonnes a year.
